A Closer Look At Asaka RikenLtd's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, Asaka RikenLtd had an accrual ratio of 0.42. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of JP¥2.6b, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of JP¥800.0m. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of JP¥2.6b, this year, indicates high risk. data.title: Baidu Is Down 59% Even Though It Turned A Profit
data.description:
Baidu has just rolled out ERNIE 5.5, a new Token Exchange marketplace, and wider Apollo Go coverage, all pitched as proof that its AI shift is gathering pace. For Baidu shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 58.8%, including dividends. If you had put money into the stock on 1 January 2026, how do these ambitious AI launches compare with that result, and which expectation now deserves the closest scrutiny?

The move put Baidu in the middle of this trade. Scan 52 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Two Baidu Stories Investors Had To Choose Between

The shares cost US$131 at the start of the period. Anyone backing Baidu then had to decide whether the company was an AI-led reinvention story or a cash-hungry transition with unclear payback.

The bullish view saw a Fair Value of US$146, a notional target based on Baidu's generative AI, Apollo Go and an assumed P/E of 18.5x on 2028 earnings, even as margins were expected to fall from 20.5% to 14.3%.

The more cautious Narrative set Fair Value at US$118, again an implied price built on 4.8% revenue growth and concern that costly AI investment and negative free cash flow could keep pressure on profitability.

What The Baidu Evidence Actually Tested

Baidu’s launch of ERNIE 5.5, the Tianchi Supernode and a busy Token Exchange supported the bullish claim that an integrated AI stack could reshape the business mix. Q3 2026 results presented a tougher story. Revenue slipped while net margin moved from a 36.0% loss in Q3 2025 to a 4.5% profit. Overall, the evidence pointed in both directions.

The lesson is clear. When an AI story is central, treat segment mix and net margin as the key test. Track how quickly new AI lines replace legacy revenue and how that affects profitability.

What Today’s Baidu Price Is Really Asking You

Baidu now trades at US$61.9, after a 58.8% loss from the start of the year. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St sets its Fair Value above that level, based on the idea that AI cloud, search and Apollo Go eventually carry more of the earnings load.

For that higher figure to hold, a buyer today would need to believe Baidu’s AI driven businesses can generate sustained, profitable revenue that outweighs pressure on traditional online marketing and heavier AI spending.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Baidu converts its AI leadership in cloud infrastructure, search monetisation and Apollo Go into sustained, profitable revenue that more than offsets pressure on traditional online marketing and higher AI investment."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Looking Beyond Baidu’s AI Push

Baidu is trying to show that full stack AI can support more earnings. You could also step back and ask where similar AI spending is already flowing.

Many customers investing in AI tools still need dependable cloud infrastructure and productivity software that blend those models into daily workflows.

One large US based group supplies that backbone, bundling AI assistants into search, office apps and enterprise data platforms.

The interesting angle is how that provider now earns from both the AI infrastructure itself and the ad and app ecosystems that sit above it.
